page: Microsoft Azure D128pds_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv7 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 128 dedicated 64-bit ARM (arm64) vCPUs paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

A primary hardware feature of the D128pds_v7 is its bundled high-capacity local storage, delivering 7,560 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state drive space. In addition to local scratch space, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring users to route external traffic via configured virtual network gateways or secondary addressing.

Because the underlying processing units utilize an ARM64 architecture, workloads requiring x86 instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, or AMX cannot execute without emulation. However, the high core count of 128 dedicated ARM vCPUs coupled with generous memory and NVMe capacity provides strong resource density and operational cost efficiency for horizontally scalable or multi-threaded software compiled for ARM.

The D128pds_v7 is structured for compute-heavy, memory-balanced applications requiring fast, low-latency access to extensive local temporary storage. Key workload targets include high-throughput relational and non-relational database management systems, distributed data processing, ETL pipelines, large software build farms, and dense multi-tenant application hosting environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D128pds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine in the Dpdsv7 series, powered by Microsoft Hyper-V and 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance features 128 dedicated arm64 vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware provisioning includes 7,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and full support for Premium Storage, without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Lacking x86-specific instruction sets, the platform requires ARM-native application stacks. The combination of dense multicore CPU allocation, 512 GB of memory, and fast local NVMe storage provides high density and efficient resource utilization for scale-out workloads. The server fits high-capacity database systems, large-scale data processing pipelines, distributed caching layers, continuous integration build clusters, and high-concurrency enterprise web applications requiring rapid temporary storage access.
